analysis.subject: physics
analysis.pageCoverage: Page covers how gravity causes constant acceleration in a vacuum, formulas linking velocity and displacement to time, a table of values at 1 second intervals, and Galileo findings about mass and air resistance.

overview.headline: Free fall under constant gravity in a vacuum

keyPoints.point: Free falling objects in a vacuum are acted on by only the gravitational force as weight.
keyPoints.quote: An object that falls through a vacuum is subjected to only one external force, the gravitational force, expressed as the weight of the object.

keyPoints.point: Gravitational acceleration near sea level on Earth is constant at 9.8 meters per square second.
keyPoints.quote: The acceleration is constant and equal to the gravitational acceleration g which is 9.8 meters per square second at sea level on the Earth.

keyPoints.point: Velocity and location of a free falling object can be determined from acceleration and time using equations.
keyPoints.quote: Knowing the acceleration, we can determine the velocity and location of any free falling object at any time using the following equations.

keyPoints.point: During free fall acceleration stays constant while velocity increases linearly and location increases quadratically.
keyPoints.quote: Notice that the acceleration is a constant, the velocity increases linearly, and the location increases quadratically.
